audit.why: 60.87% over 23 games with a chart that is mostly Skill and gives Akshan level 1 and the very late stage. The prose frames it as a range war Akshan wins until Urgot's durability arrives, which fits.
Lvl 2-3 range advantage, Lvl 6, Youmuu's, and Urgot's 2+ item durability window. Correctly placed; only the level-6 content needed rewriting.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three problems. (1) The page says you beat Fear Beyond Death by firing Comeuppance 'from outside his reach' — both ultimates are 2500 range, so there is no range advantage to take. (2) Disdain's shield is never mentioned, which changes the all-in maths on the one ability the whole lane is played around. (3) Purge's targeting rule is absent: it prioritises champions Urgot has recently struck with another ability, so eating a Corrosive Charge is what aims the shotgun at you.
audit.why: Riot's text: Fear Beyond Death range 2500; Comeuppance range 2500. Disdain — 'charges in a direction, SHIELDING HIMSELF and trampling non-champion enemies. If he catches an enemy champion, he will stop and hurl them out of his way.' Purge — 'Prioritizes enemy champions Urgot has recently struck with other abilities and triggers Echoing Flames.' Telling the reader to win the ultimate race by standing further away sends them to do something the ranges make impossible; the actual race is on health thresholds.
audit.corrected: Both ultimates reach 2500 — the race is whoever is nearer their execute threshold, not whoever stands further back. Disdain (E, 475 range, 16s) shields him as he charges. Getting hit by Corrosive Charge (Q) is what makes Purge lock onto you.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Bait his E flip on cooldown' with no number, in a lane whose entire commit timing is that one cooldown.
audit.why: Disdain is 16/15.5/15/14.5/14s — a very long window for a ranged champion to take the wave and poke freely, and worth stating.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page asserts 'Q/W percent-max-HP shred' in three places. Riot's descriptions for Corrosive Charge, Purge and Echoing Flames all say physical damage with no max-health component, and the _missing file did not flag Urgot as invalidating resistances.
audit.why: I could not confirm the percent-max-health claim from any local source, so I removed the characterisation rather than restate it, and described what the text does support: Purge's targeting priority and Echoing Flames triggering off it. I did not assert the opposite either.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the verified Purge/Echoing Flames behaviour.

edits.before: Urgot's early game is his Q/W shotgun legs, but they're short-range — and contrary to what people think, his W (Purge) doesn't root him in place, he can still walk (slowed) while shredding. The point is his damage window is point-blank, so stand outside it and pepper his giant HP bar with Q boomerang and your double-shot passive. The one thing to fear is his E (Disdain): a dash-flip that vaults you over him into shotgun range, so never trade standing next to a wall he can flip you into. He concedes Level 1 like you do, but from Level 2 your range and the extra passive shot chip him for free.
edits.after: Urgot's early game is Corrosive Charge and his legs, but they're short-range — and contrary to what people think, Purge (W, 490 range) doesn't root him in place, he walks slowed while shredding. It also PRIORITISES champions he has recently hit with another ability, so eating a Q is what aims the shotgun at you. Stand outside that range and pepper his giant HP bar with Q boomerang and your double-shot passive. Fear Disdain (E, 475 range, 16s): it shields him on the way in and hurls you out of his way, so never trade beside a wall he can pin you against.

edits.before: This is your window. With E (Heroic Swing) you get a poke-and-escape he can't answer — bait his Disdain flip, swing in once it's down, and stack your third-hit passive shield before he can re-toggle his legs. At 6, Comeuppance locks on and the missing-HP scaling lets you finish him from range, which beats his R: he wants to drop you low and chain his execute, but if you fire Comeuppance first from outside his reach he never gets there. Your first-item lethality spike is the moment to take over the lane.
edits.after: This is your window. edits.before: Two items in is where Urgot reclaims this. He stacks HP and resistances until your lethality barely scratches him, and one landed E flip drops you into his Q/W shotgun legs where the percent-max-HP shred chews through your squishy frame in a sustained fight — and his R execute closes it once you're low. You have to win this before that: convert your mid-game lead, roam with camo W to snowball other lanes, and take towers so the game never reaches the point where his percent-HP and your missing durability decide it.
edits.after: Two items in is where Urgot reclaims this. notes: The page told the reader to beat Fear Beyond Death by firing Comeuppance 'from outside his reach'. Both ultimates are 2500 range, so that plan does not exist — the exchange is decided by who is nearer their execute threshold, and that is what the page now says. Also added Disdain's self-shield (it changes whether your burst window is real) and Purge's targeting priority, which is the mechanic that explains why eating a Corrosive Charge is what gets you shredded.
unverified: The old text called Urgot's Q and W a 'percent-max-HP shred' in three places. Nothing in Riot's Data Dragon description of Corrosive Charge, Purge or Echoing Flames mentions max-health scaling, and the _missing file does not flag Urgot under resistances-invalidated, so I removed the characterisation rather than repeat it. If Purge does scale with target max health in the live game, that is worth putting back deliberately with a source. Separately, the kit file tags Corrosive Charge with a 'dash' flag, which contradicts Riot's own description of a ground-targeted explosive charge — treated as a tooltip-parsing misfire and ignored.
